name: Velex Synth-Cotton Jeans (Threadbare)
description: Velex made affordable synth-cotton jeans for Tier 2 buyers in the 2150s and 60s. Decades of wash cycles and heavy use have left Shelf-circulating pairs nearly translucent at the knees and thighs. The waistband sags. The hems are frayed to a soft fringe. Still, the straight cut is flattering and the fabric is soft in the way only exhausted material gets.
what_it_says: You're wearing something that used to be Tier 2. A lot of life has happened since then.
worn_by: anyone who grabbed a good find at the bin
story_hooks: A batch of Velex jeans from the same production run has been circulating a single Shelf block for thirty years — the same ten pairs, traded and repaired endlessly.
Someone has carefully embroidered a map on the inner thigh of a pair — it leads somewhere, if you know the neighborhood.

physical_description.visual_profile: Classic straight-leg silhouette with a lived-in slouch; the waistband sits naturally low on the hips. Despite decades of wear, the cut remains flattering and intentional-looking. The fabric drapes with soft heaviness, pooling slightly at the ankles.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed straight leg, mid-rise with natural sag at waistband. Not tight, not baggy — the ease of something worn into comfort rather than purchased that way.
physical_description.primary_material: Synth-cotton blend (60% synthetic polymer, 40% reclaimed organic fiber) — the formula Velex used in the 2150s before discontinuation
physical_description.texture: Incredibly soft and pilled from age; the weave is loose and almost gauzy at stress points. Knees and inner thighs are translucent, showing faint shadowing of skin or underlying layers. Hems fray into soft, naturally separated threads. The fabric has a lived, velvet-like quality from repeated washing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Indigo faded to dusty periwinkle and pale denim gray; darker saturated color at seams and interior. Scattered bleach stains and brownish wear marks at pocket edges and fly. Lighter areas where sweat and friction have aged the dye.
physical_description.closures: Traditional five-button fly with worn brass buttons; waistband has a single S-curve anchor point where metal has oxidized green. No zipper, no modern magnetic snaps.
distinctive_features: Translucent panels at knees and upper thighs exposing underlying fabric or skin
Frayed hem edges that naturally separate into soft fringe rather than a clean line
Sagging waistband with visible fabric relaxation at sides
Velex brand tag still visible inside waistband, text faded but readable
Worn coin pocket with darker patina
Stress whitening around pocket openings and upper thigh
Faint cross-hatch pattern from being dried on wire racks rather than machine dried
physical_description.tier_indicator: Originally Tier 2 luxury-adjacent (affordable quality denim for mid-grade workers). Now worn by Tier 3-4 as heritage/retro or Tier 5 by accident of salvage.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing these signals nostalgia, thrift, or genuine poverty dressed as aesthetic choice. Corpo kids buy reproductions; street workers actually own worn pairs. The fraying and transparency read as either 'I found these' or 'I'm ironic enough to wear degraded fabric on purpose.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily worn, soft, translucent at stress points, frayed hems, sagging waistband. Not falling apart, but clearly approaching the end of functional life. Each pair is slightly different depending on wearer and wash history.

image_prompt: Overhead fashion shot of threadbare Velex synth-cotton jeans draped on a dark matte mannequin, legs slightly splayed. Harsh neon-blue side lighting reveals translucent fabric at knees glowing pale indigo against dark background. Close detail of frayed hem showing individual separated threads in sharp focus. Moody GLMZ warehouse aesthetic — concrete, scattered coolant drips, faint holo-advertisement flicker in soft background. Dust particles visible in light.
